closed.evidence: ClientboundUpdateAdvancementsPacket: 26.2 sends plain AdvancementHolders (AdvancementHolder.LIST_STREAM_CODEC), 26.3 sends PositionedAdvancement with x/y floats per entry; 26.2 AdvancementNode has no x/y at all. Ported: dropped x/y from the protocol Advancement struct and codec (read+write), from the server's write_advancement (lan/advancements.rs, layout field removed), and from remote_advancements; the screen now always uses tree.layout() (26.2 repositionNodes) and visibility keys on remote.is_some() instead of positions. grant verified 26.2-form already (loot as keys resolved via registries, plain drop with no pickup delay); decorateName/toast diffs are getter renames only; trigger's ContextAwarePredicate vs LootItemCondition-Holder difference is below the Rust's predicate abstraction; no root-background validation exists in the Rust. The layout function's own 26.2 fidelity is item 10's scope (AdvancementTree.repositionNodes).

StrongholdPieces: StructurePiecesBuilder renamed to StructurePieceAccessor (26.2's name) with identical logic, including PortalRoom.createPiece and the 112-block bound. StrongholdStructure.generatePieces: empty diff. FixedBiomeSource: BiomeResolver/createResolver vs NoiseBiomeSource/getNoiseBiome is an API-shape change; findBiomeHorizontal and getBiomesWithin bodies are identical (single biome, allowed-test). No behavioural difference anywhere in the item.

GrassBlock.performBonemeal: 26.2 rolls the tall-grass chance as random.nextInt(10)==0 and the flower chance as random.nextInt(8)==0; 26.3 uses nextFloat()<0.1F and nextFloat()<0.125F — same probabilities but different RNG draws, so the sequence diverges after them. Ported grass_bonemeal_effect to next_int(10)==0 / next_int(8)==0 in the same short-circuit positions. The offset walk already used next_int(3)-1 (26.2's form; 26.3's nextIntBetweenInclusive draws identically). SeaPickle/GrowingPlantHead/BoneMealItem diffs are the BonemealSource parameter (26.3-only, signature only) and setBlockAndUpdate vs setBlock(...,3) (identical); the Rust has no source parameter. The flower/grass placement structure (ConfiguredFeature, empty-list fall-through) already matches 26.2.

CloudRenderer#prepare + #renderOit: 26.3 split 26.2's render() into prepare() (compute + build mesh) + render()/renderOit() (draw, incl. the new OIT path) and moved the render API from Blaze3D to RenderPearl. The geometry the Rust ports — radius cells (range*16/12), cloud offset (gameTime % (width*400) + partialTicks), cell math — is identical in both versions.

AbstractFurnaceBlockEntity: 26.2 has no speedMultiplier (field, save key and getSpeedMultiplier all 26.3-only); save times are shorts (getShortOr/putShort), not ints; getBurnDuration takes FuelValues only (no cooking_fuel component); consumeFuel takes no level/pos and drops nothing (remainder takes the slot only once the stack is used up, else lost); completion is cookingTimer == cookingTotalTime (26.3 uses >=); getTotalCookTime is the recipe's cookingTime directly. Ported: removed Furnace.speed, the drops param from FurnaceCooking::tick, Providers.speed; save/NBT canonicalisation use shorts; completion ==; furnace_fixture drops speed. canTakeItemThroughFace (water_bucket|bucket) and canPlaceItem (burn_time > 0) were already 26.2-form in machines.rs. Gap: VanillaFurnaceOracle still reflects speedMultiplier, so the furnace harness cannot run against 26.2 until the oracle + driver are ported.

SignText#hasAnyClickCommands: 26.3 takes (boolean shouldFilter), 26.2 takes (Player player) and reads player.isTextFilteringEnabled(); both scan getMessages(filter) for a RUN_COMMAND click event. The Rust has_any_click_commands checks the stored click events and keeps no filtered text, so the filter source is unobservable in either version.

MeshData#decodeQuadCentroids: bodies byte-identical between 26.3 and 26.2 (opposite-corner midpoint); the added/removed flag is only the VertexFormat type moving from com.mojang.renderpearl.api.vertex to com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex. The Rust references it in a comment only (translucency.rs:4).

Ingredient#display: 26.3 always returns TagSlotDisplay; 26.2 returns TagSlotDisplay for tags and Composite(per-item displays) for lists. The tree already decodes Composite (protocol SlotDisplay::Composite) and the resolver flattens it in order (recipe_book.rs:757), so both wire forms yield the same ordered item list the local Ingredient.order already keeps.

SignatureValidator#from: the only 26.3->26.2 diff is the authlib package move (com.mojang.authlib.services -> com.mojang.authlib.yggdrasil); both from overloads are byte-identical. The Rust references it in a comment only (secure_chat.rs:47).

Biome#getHeightAdjustedTemperature: 26.3 samples SimplexNoise(discard=true).get(x,z); 26.2 samples PerlinSimplexNoise([0]).getValue(x,z,false). Both are a single simplex octave, seed 1234, no offsets: PerlinSimplexNoise valueFactor is 1.0 for one octave, the 2D sampling math is identical (70.0 * corner sum), and both constructors consume the same random sequence (3x nextDouble, 256x nextInt shuffle; GradientNoise confirms the 26.3 order). The Rust SimplexNoise::with_skipped_offsets(1234) + get2 matches both; only a float-vs-double return (<=1 ulp, unobservable through the 0.15 snow threshold) differs.

FileToIdConverter#listMatchingResources: 26.3 routes through an extensionSelector() helper and added prefixMatches/matches; 26.2 calls manager.listResources(prefix, this::extensionMatches) directly. Same prefix, same predicate, identical behaviour. The Rust references it in a comment only (lan/data.rs:186).

GuiEntityRenderer#renderToTexture: the only 26.3->26.2 diff is PoseStack.rotate(quaternion) vs mulPose(quaternion) — a rename of the same pose multiply. The Rust emit_preview takes pre-transformed quads and ports no rotation.

Display#getInterpolatedBoundingBox exists only in 26.3 (culling box shifted by the interpolated position delta); 26.2 has getBoundingBoxForCulling() returning the raw box at the tick position. PORTED: both display_in_view call sites now pass display.position (tick) instead of the interpolated render position; the geometry still renders interpolated. Doc comment updated.

BiomeManager#getBiome: 26.3 split the BlockPos form into a delegating overload plus getBiome(int,int,int) and renamed BiomeResolver to NoiseBiomeSource; the body (x-2, >>2 zoom) is identical. The Rust ports the lookup in mesher.rs unchanged.

PatchedDataComponentMap#set: 26.3 stores the patch as raw Object with a Removed sentinel, 26.2 as Optional (empty = removed). The set/remove semantics are identical: value==default drops the patch entry, otherwise the value is stored, and the return is the previous value or the default. The Rust's comments (stations.rs:487,608,750) describe semantics true in both versions.
JumpableVehicleBar#extractBackground: the decompiled classes are identical between 26.3 and 26.2 (the changed flag is a bytecode-level artefact); the Rust jump_bar ports it unchanged.

Items#mapProperties exists only in 26.3 (a helper returning MAP_DECORATIONS EMPTY); 26.2 registers FILLED_MAP inline with MAP_DECORATIONS EMPTY plus MAP_COLOR DEFAULT (4603950). The empty-decorations elision in encode_components holds in both versions; the prototype's map_color comes from the 26.2 prepared data. Comment updated to the 26.2 registration.

ClockManager#getInstance exists only in 26.3 (returns a ClockInstance); 26.2's interface has getTotalTicks(Holder<WorldClock>) returning the ticks directly — same observable value, API shape only. All four 26.2 timelines use clock minecraft:overworld, whose total ticks are the day time, so the Rust clock callback (|_clock| at.day_time) is exactly right. Comment updated to the 26.2 API.

Pack#readPackMetadata: bodies identical except 26.3 opens via resources.openMetadata (PackMetadataResources) and 26.2 via resources.openPrimary (PackResources) — a 26.3 API split; the metadata parsing logic is unchanged. The Rust references it in a comment only (datapack.rs:172).

DebugLevelSource#buildTerrain exists only in 26.3 (ChunkGenerator step restructure); 26.2 has fillFromNoise returning the chunk unchanged plus an empty buildSurface — both no-ops, same as 26.3's buildTerrain. The Rust builds the debug chunk directly; comment updated to the 26.2 step names.

TextDisplayRenderer#submitInner: 26.2 inlines the background as custom geometry at TEXT_BACKGROUND_OFFSET (-0.01) and orders text after it; 26.3 uses submitTextBackground plus the same POLYGON_OFFSET/SEE_THROUGH text modes. The Rust draws the background quad at depth -0.01 (text_display.rs draw) and the text on the polygon-offset layer, background first — matching 26.2's observable geometry. Comment updated to the 26.2 form.

ChiseledBookShelfBlockEntity#updateState: 26.3 calls level.setBlockAndUpdate, 26.2 calls level.setBlock(pos, state, 3). Bytecode confirms setBlockAndUpdate == setBlock(..., 3) in both versions. The Rust uses flags::UPDATE_ALL (3). Comment updated.

ProtoChunk#setBlockState: 26.3 updates existing heightmaps inline then primes the missing ones; 26.2 collects the missing ones, primes, then updates ALL. Observationally equivalent: after priming from current state (which includes the new block), update() is a no-op — an opaque new block is already below firstAvailable, and a non-opaque one either returns early or rescans to the same height (verified against 26.2 Heightmap.update/primeHeightmaps). The Rust follows the 26.3 order. Bonus: 26.2's Heightmap predicate is BlockStateBase::blocksMotion (not the 26.3 tag), confirming the per-state motion port.

InputQuirks#isQuitShortcutDown exists only in 26.3 (SDL-era InputQuirks); 26.2's class is the older GLFW-era form without it. The Rust function serves the Horizon quit_shortcuts setting (allow platform quit shortcuts to close the window), and the keys (Cmd+Q macOS, Alt+F4 elsewhere) are platform conventions, not version-specific vanilla behaviour. Function kept; comment updated to note the 26.3-only provenance.

Heightmap#primeHeightmaps: 26.3 uses index-based removal from a copied list, 26.2 an iterator with back(size) rewind — the same top-down scan (first non-air state matching each type's predicate sets height y+1, break when all found). The predicate differs (26.3 tag vs 26.2 blocksMotion), already handled by the per-state motion port feeding the Rust predicates. The Rust prime() implements the same scan.

OverlayRecipeComponent#extractRenderState decompiles identically in 26.3 and 26.2. The class's only diff is mouseClicked's button constant (1 in 26.3 SDL, 0 in 26.2 GLFW — both mean left button), a method this item does not name and the Rust does not port (recipe_book_screen.rs draws the overlay; input uses winit buttons).
CrafterScreen#extractBackground: the decompiled classes are identical between 26.3 and 26.2 (the changed flag is a bytecode-level artefact); the Rust crafter() ports it unchanged.

StreamCodec#composite: 26.3 added 13- and 14-arity overloads (Function13/14); the 1-12 arity overloads are identical. The Rust packet! macro mirrors composite for any field count, so the added overloads are irrelevant.

WardenSpawnTracker#tryWarn: 26.2's ServerPlayer.getWardenSpawnTracker returns Optional<WardenSpawnTracker>, 26.3's returns the tracker directly — but 26.2's is always Optional.of(tracker), never empty, so the .map/.flatMap/.ifPresent calls are equivalent to direct calls. The Rust try_warn over a tracker slice matches both.

CreakingHeartBlockEntity#serverTick: the only 26.3->26.2 diff is setBlockAndUpdate -> setBlock(pos, state, 3) in two places, proven identical by bytecode (item 253). The Rust ports serverTick's logic unchanged.

TitleScreen#init: 26.3 adds an isOfflineDeveloperMode() check to the friends button and drops a constructor arg from OptionsScreen; neither changes the buttons' add order or positions, which is all key_focus.rs ports (tab-order test).

PathNavigation#moveTo: 26.3 added a moveTo(Entity, int reachRange, double) overload; 26.2's moveTo(Entity, double) inlines createPath(target, 1). The 2-arg form is identical (reach 1). The Rust calls nav_move_to_entity(w, at, 1, speed).

PrimedTnt#tick: 26.3 added setRequiresPrecisePosition(horizontalCollision || verticalCollision) and getMoveSimulationType() (SERVER_AND_CLIENT); 26.2 has neither. The fuse/fall/bounce/smoke logic is identical, and the Rust client-side TNT tick ports that unchanged. Nuance (out of scope, negligible): 26.2's ServerEntity full-syncs TNT only when onGround changes, while the Rust lan_entities sets precise whenever on the ground (the 26.3 rule); a resting TNT's deltas are 0 either way, so nothing player-visible differs.

LevelLoadingScreen#extractBackground: the method body is identical; the class diff is only the static chunk-status colour map (26.3 TERRAIN 3159410 vs 26.2 NOISE 13750737 / SURFACE 7497737 / CARVERS 3159410), which the Rust does not port anywhere (no colour constant appears in the tree). The Rust ports only the Reason-based background.

Ravager#blockedByItem: the Ravager override is the same in both (50% stun, else fling; syncVelocity is 26.3's rename of hurtMarked; fullyBlocked unused in the body). But the base LivingEntity.blockedByItem differs: 26.3 skips the 0.5 knockback when fully blocked, 26.2 knocks back unconditionally. Ported: shield.rs blocked_by_attacker now knocks back unconditionally and the fully parameter is removed (dealDefaultKnockback's own fully-blocked gate is identical in both versions, so health.rs is untouched).

CaveVines#use: the only 26.3->26.2 diff is the loot call's signature (26.3 passes pos as an extra loot-context argument); the table (HARVEST_CAVE_VINE) and state are the same. The Rust fox port drops 1 glow berry and clears berries, matching both.

Witch#performRangedAttack: 26.3 replaced the hardcoded 8.0F uncertainty with rangedAttackUncertainty(level), which returns 8.0F for witches; the potion selection, speeds (0.45/0.75) and aim (yd + dist*0.2) are identical. The Rust uses 8.0.
SharedConstants#getProtocolVersion: the pin differs (777 in 26.3, 776 in 26.2) and the tree already carries PROTOCOL_VERSION = 776 from the ladder re-base.

ClientInformation#write: 26.3 encodes the three enums via STREAM_CODEC, 26.2 via writeEnum — both write the ordinal as a varint, same field order, same wire bytes. The Rust adapter writes varints and drops particle_status for 1.21.1, matching both.

ServerExplosion#hurtEntities: two diffs. (1) 26.3 gates damage on source.doTeamsAllowDamage(entity); 26.2 has no team check — explosions hurt team mates. Ported: removed the teams_allow closure, the player hurtable gate (explosion_hurt_player's exploding param dropped) and hurt_mob's hurtable param; the teammate test case now documents the 26.2 rule. (2) 26.3 calls pushFromExplosion, 26.2 push — but 26.3's pushFromExplosion is just push(impulse), so the Rust push_from_explosion is unchanged.

WanderingTrader#mobInteract: 26.3 returns SUCCESS_SERVER for trading, 26.2 returns SUCCESS (which swings the hand). SUCCESS_SERVER itself exists in 26.2 (spawn eggs still return it in both versions). Ported in remote_mob_use.rs: mob_swings' trader arm now swings except for spawn eggs (SUCCESS_SERVER) and leads (CONSUME), and the name-tag branch swings in both cases (unnamed falls through to trading, SUCCESS in 26.2). Test assertions added. Follow-up: the horse fedFood and panda bamboo arms in the same function still encode SUCCESS_SERVER and are unverified for 26.2 (no rank-2 item names them).

UnderwaterAmbientSoundHandler#tick: only a class rename (26.3 UnderLiquidSubSound vs 26.2 UnderwaterAmbientSoundInstances.SubSound); thresholds (1e-4/0.001/0.01), sounds and tickDelay logic are identical. The Rust tick_underwater matches both.

ItemUtils#createFilledResult: the only diff is 26.3's player.drop(stack, false, Prediction.PREDICTED) vs 26.2's player.drop(stack, false) — the Prediction argument belongs to 26.3's prediction system, which 26.2 lacks; the drop itself is identical. The Rust filled() has no Prediction concept and ports the drop unchanged.
CrafterBlockEntity#serverTick: the only diff is setBlockAndUpdate -> setBlock(pos, state, 3), proven identical by bytecode (item 253).

BeaconMenu#removed: the only diff is 26.3's player.drop(stack, false, Prediction.SERVER_ONLY) vs 26.2's player.drop(stack, false) — the Prediction argument belongs to 26.3's prediction system; the drop is identical. The Rust drops the payment with no Prediction concept.
LoomScreen#extractBackground: the decompiled classes are identical between 26.3 and 26.2 (the changed flag is a bytecode-level artefact).

ResultSlot#onTake: the only diff is 26.3's player.drop(replacement, false, Prediction.PREDICTED) vs 26.2's player.drop(replacement, false) — the Prediction argument belongs to 26.3's prediction system; the remainder drop is identical. The Rust ports the remainder handling with no Prediction concept.
ModelPart#translateAndRotate: only poseStack.rotate -> mulPose (same rename as item 217); the ZYX rotation and /16 translation are identical. The Rust applies glam EulerRot::ZYX, matching both.

PiglinAi#throwItemsTowardPos: 26.3 calls swing(OFF_HAND, SwingAnimation.DEFAULT), 26.2 calls swing(OFF_HAND) — the default animation either way (the piglin's off hand carries no swing_animation component). The Rust swings the off hand with SwingAnimation::DEFAULT.
AbstractVillager#addOffersFromTradeSet: only tradeSet.trades() -> tradeSet.getTrades() (26.3 made TradeSet a record; 26.2's class has a getter). Same offers, same duplicates handling.

Fireworks#addToTooltip: 26.3 uses translatable flight_duration with a %s argument; 26.2 builds translatable flight + SPACE + number. 26.2's lang has NO flight_duration key (only flight = 'Flight Duration:'), so the Rust's 26.3 form rendered the raw key. Ported: the flight line now uses the flight key + space + number; the test's fake lang now carries the 26.2 key. Expected lines unchanged ('Flight Duration: 1').
Phantom#tick: only the playLocalSound call form (26.3's entity overload vs 26.2's positional overload with a trailing false); same sound, same volume/pitch draws (0.95 + rand*0.05 twice).

Dolphin#registerGoals: 26.3 uses TryFindLiquidGoal with the DOLPHIN_TRIES_TO_FIND tag, 26.2 uses TryFindWaterGoal. The Rust already ports the 26.2 form (TryFindWater seeking Fluid::Water, goals.rs:2714).

LongJump#canRun: the only diff is the fluid gate — 26.3 inlines isInFluidDeeperThan(threshold, ENTITY_FLOATABLE) || isInLava(), 26.2 calls Swim.shouldSwim (isInWater && water height > threshold || isInLava). ENTITY_FLOATABLE is water only, so the gates are equivalent. The Rust uses Mob::floats() (water > threshold || in lava), matching both.

TrialSpawner$FullConfig#overrideEntityData: 26.3-only (with TrialSpawnerBlockEntity.setEntityData and BaseSpawner.setEntityData). 26.2's SpawnEggItem.useOn always calls setEntityId(type) — an op's egg data is never applied, on trial or regular spawners. Ported: spawn_egg_on_spawner returns only the id, use_spawn_egg_on_spawner drops its data parameter, override_entity_data and Spawner.set_entity_data removed (with the 26.3-only merge test, which pinned behaviour 26.2 lacks).

Font#prepareBackground: 26.3-only helper (creates the background effect at z=-0.01); 26.2's TextDisplayRenderer inlines the same -0.01 background geometry (item 252). The Rust already draws the background 0.01 behind; only the comment's citation updated to the 26.2 form.

AttributeTrackSampler#applyTimeBased: only the clock API (26.3 clockManager.getInstance(clock).totalTicks() vs 26.2 clockManager.getTotalTicks(clock)) — the same API-shape difference as item 237, same value. The Rust apply() takes the tick count as a parameter; the caller passes day time.
